title: Health-Facility Electricity Reliability In Low- And Middle-Income Countries
summary: Build a verified workflow for measuring whether health facilities have electricity that is present, functional, reliable, backup-capable, and sufficient for named services without treating a connection or solar installation as proof of safe care.
why_it_matters: A ministry of health infrastructure director, rural electrification agency, or health funder deciding between a new connection, backup power, battery or generator maintenance, load upgrades, and measurement-system support cannot allocate well from a binary electricity-access count. Verified facility- and service-area evidence could change which bottleneck receives the next infrastructure or maintenance dollar while preventing electricity access from being misrepresented as quality of care or mortality benefit.

success_metrics.target: Every output separates connection, current function, outage duration, backup availability, load capacity, service-area coverage, and maintenance status.
success_metrics.validation_method: Domain reviewer checks every measure against the source instrument, observation window, denominator, and missingness rule.

success_metrics.target: A source inventory records facility level, sampling frame, geography, source date, access conditions, outage definition, and which services or devices are observed.
success_metrics.validation_method: Run pnpm validate and have a second reviewer reconstruct each classification from evidence.md and the cited source.

success_metrics.target: At least one named setting yields a reviewed and independently replicated bottleneck table that can distinguish connection, backup, repair, or load-assessment needs without issuing a procurement order.
success_metrics.validation_method: Replicator reruns the table from a documented input hash and domain and field reviewers confirm that the decision boundary is explicit.

success_metrics.target: No canonical output claims that electricity reliability alone proves clinical quality, patient outcomes, or cost-effectiveness.
success_metrics.validation_method: Red-team and field-reality reviewers inspect outputs.md, validation.md, and each proposed use before publication.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, health-systems and energy-domain review, red-team review of procurement and clinical overreach, field-reality review of infrastructure decisions, and independent replication before any financing or service recommendation.
